## Research selection and novelty gate

Several weaker framings were rejected before settling on the report thesis.

A stack-only "better eBPF profiler" framing is too broad because production whole-system eBPF profilers already perform low-overhead cross-language stack collection. A pure `io_uring` lifecycle tracer is also too narrow because current kernel tracepoints already expose request/ring/correlation fields and recent `uringscope` work reconstructs per-request `io_uring` flows with CO-RE eBPF. Likewise, application-defined resource attribution is not an empty field: OSDI 2026 `gigiprofiler` combines semantic discovery, static validation, and runtime request-to-resource tracking, while BCC already has off-CPU/waker tools that connect some scheduler relationships.

The narrower gap survives those alternatives: no one mechanism in the inspected evidence provides a **generic sparse cross-boundary causal layer** that joins ordinary profile samples across kernel workqueue identity, scheduler wakeups, `io_uring` submission/completion, userspace runtime-task identity, and application-defined resources while preserving continuous-profiling cost semantics. The report therefore does not claim that each individual edge is novel. It asks whether a bounded handoff graph plus optional runtime joins can form a useful middle layer between stack-only profiling and full request tracing.

Primary evidence checked in this run includes Linux tracepoint/runtime sources, the OpenTelemetry Profiles specification and eBPF profiler, current Tokio task identity and Rust `tracing` semantics, Go `runtime/trace`, OSDI 2026 `gigiprofiler`, and OSDI 2026 Blink. The `uringscope` preprint and eBPF thread-dynamics work were used as adjacent counterevidence to narrow the thesis away from single-subsystem reconstruction or generic inter-thread metrics.

The measurement claim is also bounded. OSDI 2026 Blink shows that sampling can be systematically biased on flat short-routine workloads, not merely noisy. An adaptive causal profiler that changes capture probability after detecting suspicious events can create another selection effect. The report therefore treats probability-aware sampling and calibration against high-fidelity ground truth as part of the design, rather than assuming more adaptive samples automatically produce an unbiased aggregate profile.

## Validation and self-review requirements

The report starts with a concrete request whose work crosses threads and async boundaries before introducing the causal-handoff abstraction. It separates execution location, causal handoff, and semantic ownership; identifies where Linux exposes correlation identities; states where kernel-only observation stops; and includes explicit falsification conditions for each proposed mechanism.

The decisive report-level test is attribution correctness, not only collection overhead. A convincing evaluation must measure causal-edge precision/recall, request/task attribution accuracy, false joins under identifier reuse, aggregate cost-attribution error, event/state volume, and confidence-interval coverage. If exact edge capture approaches full-tracing overhead, runtime adapters require tracing-equivalent instrumentation, or modern trace context already follows nearly all relevant async work cheaply, the proposed middle layer loses its reason to exist.

Repository CI remains authoritative for generated output. The final PR head must pass all required and expected checks. After CI is green, the complete diff and generated output must receive a clean self-review before squash merge. The exact squash commit must then pass the production `Deploy Static App` workflow, and the English and Chinese routes must be verified before the merged-PR closeout comment is posted.
